status: frozen synthetic development source foundation before native bank statement activation
why: The existing bank family bank-cash-movements-1 (and its withdrawal/deposit variant) requires a prepared template carrying Record ID, Settlement ID, Role, Policy, Status and scope columns on every row. A bank statement as the bank issues it carries none of these, so today it is refused at BANK_COLUMNS whatever its format, and the bank workspace accepts only .csv and .xlsx. This foundation fixes the facts a native statement family must reproduce before any engine work.

sources.statement: Bank account statement as issued: printed PDF with a real text layer (Chromium page.pdf, DejaVu Sans embedded), one account, one currency, one period. BS01 also as statement CSV and XLSX carrying the same story.
sources.cashbook: Company cashbook export for the same account and period as CSV (UTF-8, CRLF); BS01 also as XLSX.
sources.facts: stories.json, regenerated byte for byte by `node stories.mjs` and sealed by hash, never stored. Each statement page is listed line by line as printed.

statement.Date: transaction date (yyyy-mm-dd; Arabic-Indic digits in BS11)
statement.Value Date: value date; never used for matching, only for timing
statement.Description: narrative, may wrap over lines and continue at the top of the next page; never used for matching
statement.Reference: bank reference as printed; may be empty
statement.Balance: running balance after the movement; an overdrawn balance is printed with the suffix DR

cashbook.Voucher: voucher number, unique within the cashbook
cashbook.Reference: reference the company recorded; may be empty
cashbook.Payments: money paid out of the account

fields.headers: English layout: Date, Value Date, Description, Reference, Withdrawal, Deposit, Balance. Arabic layout: التاريخ، تاريخ القيمة، البيان، المرجع، سحب، إيداع، الرصيد (right-to-left).

lines.movement: exactly one of Withdrawal or Deposit is positive; the other is empty

nonMovement.opening: Opening balance, first line of page 1
nonMovement.brought-forward: Balance brought forward, first line of every later page
nonMovement.carried-forward: Balance carried forward, last line of every page but the last
nonMovement.closing: Closing balance, on the last page
nonMovement.totals: Total withdrawals / deposits of the whole statement, last page
nonMovement.page-totals: Withdrawals / deposits of the page's own movements (BS14, BS15)
nonMovement.continuation: rest of the previous page's last description (BS08)

lines.rule: Non-movement lines are controls or text. They are never movements, never matched and never counted in totals.
lines.pageFurniture: Bank name, title, the account/currency/period line, the column headings and the `Page n of N` footer repeat on every page outside the table body. They are neither movements nor controls.

statementProof.pages: Every page states `Page n of N` with one N for the whole statement, and the pages present are exactly 1..N in order. Otherwise the statement is incomplete-pages.
statementProof.chain: Opening balance, then each movement: previous balance + deposit - withdrawal = printed balance. Brought-forward equals the previous page's carried-forward and the running balance; carried-forward equals the running balance at the end of its page; closing equals the final running balance; page totals and statement totals equal the sums of their movements. Any difference makes the statement balance-broken.
statementProof.blocking: An incomplete-pages or balance-broken statement is held: no automatic approval, no suggestion, and no item called outstanding, since a missing or misprinted page may hold its counterpart.

matching.dates: Statement transaction date against cashbook date, in calendar days.
matching.direction: Withdrawal corresponds to Payments, Deposit to Receipts.
matching.reference: Equal only when identical after trimming surrounding spaces. No prefix stripping, case folding, digit extraction or similarity.

byReference.auto: Exactly one statement movement and exactly one cashbook entry carry the reference, with the same direction, the same amount to the minor unit and dates no more than dateWindowDays apart.
byReference.direction-conflict: one movement and one entry under the reference, opposite directions
byReference.amount-difference: one movement and one entry under the reference, same direction, different amounts
byReference.date-gap: one movement and one entry under the reference, same direction and amount, dates further apart than dateWindowDays
byReference.duplicate-reference: the reference appears on both sides and more than once on at least one side; all its members go to review together

byAmountAndDate.scope: Movements and entries left after the reference step, including those whose reference has no counterpart.
byAmountAndDate.amount-date-suggestion: A movement and an entry of the same direction and amount within dateWindowDays that have no other such candidate on either side. Review only: equal amount and date never prove identity.
byAmountAndDate.ambiguous-amount-date: Several candidates connected by amount, direction and date. All go to review together; the engine picks none.

outstanding.bankOnly: statement movements left after both steps (for example a bank charge not yet booked)
outstanding.cashOnly: cashbook entries left after both steps (for example an unpresented cheque or a deposit in transit)

matching.timing: Statement movements whose value date falls outside the statement period. A flag beside the match, not a reason to refuse it.

stories.BS01: clean statement, explicit shared references; also as statement CSV/XLSX and cashbook XLSX
stories.BS02: two transfers on one day for the same amount, distinct references, listed in opposite orders
stories.BS03: bank charge on the statement only; unpresented cheque and deposit in transit in the cashbook only
stories.BS04: no reference on either side; unique amount and date
stories.BS05: same reference, amounts one halala apart
stories.BS06: same reference and amount, opposite directions
stories.BS07: one reference twice on the statement for one cashbook entry
stories.BS08: descriptions wrapped over two lines; a description continuing at the top of page 2
stories.BS09: one printed running balance off by 10.00 on the last page
stories.BS12: reference written differently on the two sides (776611 / CHQ-776611)
stories.BS13: movement on the last day with value date in the next period
stories.BS15: 100 pages with page totals; the balance runs into overdraft (DR)

counts.formatControls: BS01 statement CSV and XLSX, cashbook XLSX

textLayer: Read with an independent reader (pdfminer.six) at freeze time, see VERIFY.json. Chromium writes Arabic in visual order with presentation forms, reverses the segment order of dates in right-to-left runs, and writes the Latin ligature U+FB01 for "fi"; long descriptions wrap inside their column. A native reader must handle all of these from the text layer and its geometry, not by guessing.
gapsWithoutCase: a page whose account, currency or period differs from the other pages
an opening balance that differs from the previous period's closing (BNK-2)
a reversal or returned item pairing two statement lines (BNK-1)
notClaimed: fees, taxes or charges inferred from descriptions or from differences
several accounts or currencies in one statement
repairing a broken balance chain or a missing page
authenticity of the statement or completeness beyond its own page numbering
producers other than one synthetic writer; field formats are measured by VAL-1, not assumed here
